exchanges_white.title: Mechanize Proposition 7.1 in TLA+ — repeated game with graduated trigger, observable history, Apalache δ-sweep
exchanges_white.counter: Add a TLA+ specification of the two-agent repeated claim-signaling game with the three-round graduated trigger as the agent's local automaton, Merkle-evidence history as the shared variable, and δ ∈ {0.20, 0.25, 0.253, 0.30, 0.50, 0.90} as a discrete parameter. Property to check (Apalache, bounded model): for δ > δ★_{k=3}, no finite trace of length ≤ N admits a strictly profitable one-shot deviation from (T,T); for δ ≤ δ★_{k=3}, Apalache should produce a counter-trace at the smallest δ in the grid. Cite the artifact at the end of the deviation-analysis paragraph (~line 706 of the .tex), parallel to the existing §sec:tlaplus citations. Pair it with a Z3 SMT check of the closed-form cubic 3δ³+3δ²+3δ−1>0 so the δ★ value itself is machine-checked.

exchanges_white.title: Independently rederive the cubic — δ ≈ 0.253 verified; add a two-line derivation so the reader does not need to re-run the algebra
exchanges_white.counter: Replace the current single sentence ("...solves numerically to δ > δ★_{k=3} ≈ 0.253") with a half-paragraph derivation. Independently verified: the sustainability condition 1 < 3δ(1+δ+δ²) is equivalent to f(δ) = 3δ³ + 3δ² + 3δ − 1 > 0; evaluating at δ = 0.25 gives −1/64 ≈ −0.0156 (negative, deviation profitable), at δ = 0.253 gives f ≈ −4×10⁻⁴ (essentially zero), at δ = 0.26 gives ≈ 0.0355 (positive, deviation strictly unprofitable). The unique real root in [0,1] is δ★_{k=3} ≈ 0.25319 (Cardano or one Newton step from δ₀ = 1/4). The grim-trigger limit (k→∞) collapses the inequality to 1 < 3δ/(1−δ), i.e., δ > 1/4 exactly — recovering the standard prisoner's-dilemma folk bound. Adding this derivation defends the proposition against the "the cubic doesn't actually have a closed form" attack and against rounding-error skepticism on the 0.003 gap.

exchanges_white.title: Promote "Sybil-resistant identity regime of the Anchor Protocol" to a named, quantified hypothesis (H_anchor)
exchanges_white.counter: The proposition currently reads "Under the observable-history regime of §sec:attribution and the Sybil-resistant identity regime of the Anchor Protocol [cite], ...". Strengthen to a numbered hypothesis labelled H_anchor: "(H_anchor) There exists a trust-anchor primitive ρ such that Pr[an adversary controlling k identities under ρ] ≤ ε(k) · n⁻¹ for ε non-decreasing in k and ε(1) < δ★_{k=3} · (1 − δ) / (1 − δ^{k+1}) · (c − p)/(d − c)." State the proposition as a conditional theorem on H_anchor + observable-history. Footnote: "The Anchor Protocol companion paper [owens2026anchor] establishes H_anchor with the parameters of its §6." This converts the implicit asterisk in the v2.5 wording into a formal hypothesis with a named ε-bound, which (a) defends against the "the paper hand-waves Sybil cost" attack, and (b) makes the dependency mechanically tractable — the same TLA+ spec in WT-v25v26-001 can take H_anchor as a parameter and refuse to verify when ε is too large.

exchanges_white.title: Explicit symbol mapping from §sec:youle:a6 cartel game to the multi-oracle 2-of-3 collusion problem — and a stake variable for oracles
exchanges_white.counter: The current paragraph says "the same insurer-collusion analysis applies (§sec:youle:a6) with the oracles in the role of bidders." Strengthen by adding an explicit symbol table immediately after that sentence: insurer premium q_I ↔ oracle verdict-bias signal v_O (binary settle/slash); insurer deposit B_dep ↔ oracle stake B_dep^oracle (must be introduced — see below); insurer detection probability p_d ↔ audit sampling rate σ; one-shot deviation surplus (q_floor − q*) ↔ per-settlement collusion rent r_O; folk-theorem threshold p_d^★ ↔ σ^★. The new variable B_dep^oracle is load-bearing: the existing oracle paragraph has the audit sampling rate but no stake at risk for the gameable oracles. Add a sentence requiring Oracles 1 and 2 to post a per-settlement bond equal to at least the disputed bond B_T (or a fraction thereof, capped per A5's coverage-bound result) so that detection-via-human-audit triggers a slash whose magnitude is fixed in the same currency as the cartel rent. Without a stake variable the "same analysis applies" claim is structurally weaker than v2.5 implies because the cartel folk theorem is stake-denominated.

exchanges_white.title: Extend the §sec:youle:a6 TLA+ cartel model (carried from v2.5) with an oracle-layer variant — single artifact covers both folk theorems
exchanges_white.counter: The v2.5 dialogue carries 'cartel formal repeated-game analysis' indefinitely behind the Monte Carlo. The oracle-collusion composition claim added in v2.6 makes that carry more expensive: there are now two places (§sec:youle:a6 and §sec:pricing:settlement) leaning on one unmechanized result. Build a single TLA+ model parameterized by {layer ∈ {insurer, oracle}, n_colluders, p_d (or σ), δ, B_dep, q_floor (or r_O)} so the artifact verifies both claims at once and the paper can cite one path. Property: for σ < σ^★, the model finds an unprofitable-deviation trace; for σ ≥ σ^★, the cartel-sustaining state is unreachable from initial states under the strategy profile. Defends against the "two unmechanized folk theorems for the price of one" attack.

exchanges_white.counter: The threat-class table introduces three concrete bond bands without simulation evidence. The v2.5 dialogue already ships proofs/bonded/pareto/simulation.mjs with 36-config Monte Carlo; extend it with a threat-mix dimension (proportion of careless / abandoning / sabotage agents) and verify, for each band, that (a) commons-deficit converges to zero, and (b) participation rate stays above the bootstrap Phase-2 50% retention floor. exchanges_white.title: Cite marketplace cold-start literature OR mark 80/50/60 as calibrated-from-deployments with explicit revision policy
exchanges_white.counter: The three transition metrics (Phase 1 ≥ 80% completion, Phase 2 ≥ 50% retention, Phase 3 ≥ 60% repeat-poster rate) appear without provenance. Two acceptable defenses: (a) cite Evans & Schmalensee 2010 ('Failure to launch: critical mass in platform businesses'), Hagiu & Wright 2015 ('Multi-sided platforms'), and Rochet & Tirole 2003 ('Platform competition in two-sided markets') at the relevant phase paragraphs — these are the canonical works on platform cold-start thresholds; OR (b) replace the bare percentages with a half-sentence: "Starting target bands, calibrated from observed cold-start deployments [refs]; revision policy: any phase whose threshold is missed for ≥ N consecutive measurement windows triggers a parameter review (see appendix A.X)." Pick one; the v2.5 wording ("Below this threshold the cohort is not yet generating usable risk signal") gestures at the right intuition but leaves the number itself indefensible. The Evans-Schmalensee / Hagiu citations are the lower-cost option and they exist.

exchanges_white.section: \S\ref{sec:correlating-device} ("price of anarchy" sentence at line ~295) + Abstract
exchanges_white.title: PoA ≈ 1 claim — keep the existing hedge but propagate it to the abstract; today the abstract overclaims
exchanges_white.counter: Line 295 already has the correct hedge: "in the limit where bonds cover full cleanup cost and reputation noise is bounded ... The analytical bound under realistic reputation noise is open; we do not close it here." The abstract is more aggressive: "the price of anarchy stays bounded at both layers." These are not equivalent — 'bounded' suggests an analytical bound exists at both layers, which the body explicitly disclaims. Edit the abstract sentence to: "...so the price of anarchy is empirically near 1 in calibrated regimes (σ_r ≤ 0.1) and is bounded by the cartel folk-theorem threshold σ^★ at the insurer layer; the analytical bound for the agent layer under general reputation noise is open." Matches the body, defends against the obvious red-team move of quoting the abstract against the body. The hedge already exists in one location; this propagates it to the other.

exchanges_white.section: \S\ref{sec:claim-signaling-ic} ("What each condition buys" bullet list, lines 719–726)
exchanges_white.title: Keep the conditions-list at full length — every bullet is load-bearing for a specific red-team class
exchanges_white.counter: The merge agent flagged this 8-line block as cuttable. Defending the keep, with one-sentence justification per bullet: bullet 1 (observable history) closes the §sec:attribution coupling attack; bullet 2 (Anchor) closes the Sybil-reset attack and is the cite-target for WT-v25v26-003's H_anchor formalization; bullet 3 (δ < 0.253) closes the short-lived-principal attack and forward-references §sec:economic pricing; bullet 4 (δ < 1/4) closes the "folk theorem won't save you" attack. Each bullet is one of the four standard challenges to a repeated-game IC result; removing any one reopens an attack surface. Cost is ~8 lines of an already 46-page paper, which is below the noise floor. Action: keep as-is, add a one-line preface — "Each of the following bullets defends against a specific failure mode the proposition implicitly assumes away; cutting any bullet reopens the corresponding attack." Pick keep; do not also complain.
